newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures begin pit trading lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures begin pit trading lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures gave up a small portion of Tuesday's gains early, dragged down by revived worries that the economy is expanding too quickly to avoid a rate hike to guard against an upswing in inflation.
U.S. Treasury bond futures retreated to moderate losses after first-quarter U.S. gross domestic product surged 5.6 percent, well above forecasts for a 4.1-percent growth rate.
The price index increased at a 2.7-percent clip and the deflator grew at a 2.3-percent pace.
Traders waited to see whether April's Chicago purchasing manager's index, seen at 56.2, refutes or confirms the growth.

Traders said Wednesday morning's data shifted sentiment nearly 180 degrees from Tuesday's "no-rate-hike" euphoria that launched June S&P 500 futures to one of their biggest single-day point gains ever.
"It's a flip of the coin here," said one Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures trader. "We've gone from no rate hike or a minimal one, to a rate hike."

Nearby S&P 500s rallied 24.60 points Tuesday after a tamer-than-expected reading in the employment cost index and a drop in durable goods orders quelled talk of a likely rate hike at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting May 20.
"It's quite a different atttitude from yesterday," agreed another floor broker. "We're not so bad right now. We're settling in."
Brokers said dealers sold at the opening, with locals actively taking the other side. But subsequent loss-cutting in T-bond futures lifted some of the pressure in stock futures.
Futures barely wobbled after the April Chicago purchasing managers index slipped to 57.2 from 57.5 and against forecasts for 56.2. Prices fell to 53.3, and employment rose to 56.1.
"We thought it (Chicago purchasers' index) would give us a little shake, but it didn't do much," the broker added.
